title.value: Forecasting Sensor Values in Waste-To-Fuel Plants: a Case Study
title.justification: The title is clearly mentioned at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: Forecasting Sensor Values in Waste-To-Fuel Plants: a Case Study.

extractions.description: This research paper develops machine learning models to predict future sensor readings of a waste-to-fuel plant, enabling proactive control of the plant's operations. The study involves different modeling approaches to predict sensor values based on historical data from a real-world use case in Canada. The aim is to facilitate better optimization, control, and decision-making in waste-to-fuel production processes that convert organic waste into high-quality diesel.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on optimizing waste-to-fuel processes, emphasizing better waste management and reducing reliance on fossil fuels, which are key elements of sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Organic wastes in energy conversion technologies are an active area of research aimed at reducing dependence on fossil fuels, optimizing production costs, improving waste management, and controlling emissions.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the study is on waste-to-fuel conversion processes, optimizing these operations to manage waste more effectively while producing synthetic diesel from organic waste, addressing waste issues which align under Pollution.
primary_category.quote: The JEMS waste-to-fuel plant produces synthetic diesel (SynDi) from any hydrocarbon-based waste, such as wood, biomass, paper, waste fuels and oils, plastics, textiles, rubber, and agricultural residues.

secondary_categories.justification: The study supports climate change mitigation by focusing on waste-to-fuel processes which reduce emissions and reliance on fossil fuels.
secondary_categories.quote: Organic wastes in energy conversion technologies are an active area of research aimed at reducing dependence on fossil fuels, optimizing production costs, improving waste management, and controlling emissions.

primary_sub_category.justification: The central theme revolves around using waste-to-fuel technology to manage waste, optimize processes, and produce biofuel, which fits within the Waste sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: The plant uses a chemical-catalytic de-polymerization process, the advantage of which is that the temperature is too low to produce carcinogenic gasses. It operates continuously and produces about 150 liters of fuel per hour.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The application of machine learning in optimizing process control in the waste-to-fuel industry highlights its secondary focus on industrial process improvement.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: This research, we develop machine learning models to predict future sensor readings of a waste-to-fuel plant, which would enable proactive control of the plant’s operations.
